Following our customer kickoff, attaching the implementation checklist we promised (aurora-implementation-checklist.xlsx). BrightBridge is ready to start the two-week integration sprint focused on SDK initialization, endpoint migration (sandbox -> prod), and throttling safeguards. High-level asks from the customer: sample SDKs (Node + Python), clear retry/timeouts guidance, and an endpoint migration plan that limits user impact.

What we need from the technical side this week:
- A short runbook for SDK setup + config defaults (Marcus)
- Concrete sample snippets for Node and Python (Vanessa)
- A migration checklist for switching traffic to the new call path (dual-write/canary ideas welcome)
- Recommended timeout and retry parameters, and guidance for 429/503 behavior

Proposed SLA/targets the customer mentioned: p95 latency target near 200ms; baseline steady-state 100 req/s but with bursty traffic during business hours.

Can you review and drop a first-pass plan by EOD today? Also, can we lock a 30-minute technical handoff tomorrow (Fri) at 10:00 AM PT with Rachel and Alex? I will own the call invite.

Thanks Monica — great summary. Quick technical plan below, I will push the code artifacts to the shared repo and attach a zip for immediate review (sdk-snippets-aurora.zip).

1) SDK init and config defaults
- auth: API key + optional mTLS if BrightBridge wants VPC/VPN (documented in endpoint-migration-playbook.md)
- default timeouts: connect_timeout=2000ms, read_timeout=15000ms
- concurrency guidance: recommend client pool size based on expected QPS; start with pool=10 for 100req/s and tune

2) Retry policy (recommended)
- Idempotent requests (GET, HEAD): retry up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff (base=250ms) and full jitter
- Non-idempotent (POST): use idempotency_token header; retry up to 3 attempts only when response indicates safe to retry (e.g., network errors, 502/504), avoid retrying on 4xx except 429
- Respect Retry-After header when present

3) 429 and rate-limit strategy
- Client: implement a leaky-bucket + token bucket local limiter to smooth spikes and avoid immediate replays
- Server: Redwood will send standard x-rate-limit headers and Retry-After; we recommend client honor those and fall back to reduced-model variant for degraded periods (smaller model type to preserve latency)

4) Endpoint migration approach
- Sandbox -> dual-write to sandbox and staging API endpoints for 48h (collect telemetry)
- Canary: 5% traffic 24h, 25% 24h, full cutover if error/latency within SLOs
- Rollback trigger: p95 latency increase >30% or error rate >1% absolute for two windows in a row

I'll attach the endpoint migration playbook and a small sample showing SDK init for Node and Python. Will also include a simple backoff helper in the snippets.

-Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
